# CShapes 2.0 display derivative

CShapes by Guy Schvitz, Seraina Rüegger, Luc Girardin, Lars-Erik Cederman, Nils Weidmann and Kristian Skrede Gleditsch, ETH Zürich International Conflict Research.

Source: https://icr.ethz.ch/data/cshapes/
Original GeoJSON: https://icr.ethz.ch/data/cshapes/CShapes-2.0.geojson
License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/

Cite: Schvitz et al. (2022). “Mapping the International System, 1886–2019: The CShapes 2.0 Dataset.” Journal of Conflict Resolution 66(1):144–161. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1177/00220027211013563

The files `cshapes-periods-v7.geojson` and any shards declared in its manifest are a dataset derivative under the same CC BY-NC-SA-4.0 license. They are not included in the application's MIT license or any general narrative-content license. The site is an educational noncommercial atlas. Commercial reuse of this layer requires a compatible permission from its rights holders.

Changes by World History Atlas: geometry rounded and simplified for display; ring orientation normalized for D3; source country-period date components retained; English/Chinese display labels, source notes, source links and deterministic colors added. Annual selection uses 31 December; selected historical labels are separate from the source's alias labels. Dataset source SHA-256 and simplification settings are in the GeoJSON metadata.

This is a source-coded international boundary dataset. Dependencies are included. Do not infer sovereignty or independence from the presence of a polygon. It does not reconstruct every disputed claim or wartime front. Small changes and changes reversed after war may not be represented under the source's coding policy.
